newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade mulls Thai reports.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade mulls Thai reports.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Tuesday as the trade pondered reports on the meeting between the Thai government and rubber farmers on its intervention in the market, dealers said.
A rubber market official in Thailand said the meeting on Monday evening was to discuss the mechanics of the intervention plan approved earlier by the Thai cabinet.
"The scheme will end on July 31 and the government has earmarked 4.7 billion baht for this intervention plan. They already started and the scheme will go ahead as planned," the official said.

Bangkok is intervening in the market by buying rubber at 29 baht a kg from 27.50 baht previously to prop up the market. "We'd want to see more details of the plan come out," one dealer in Singapore said. "The meeting should flesh it out."
Trading in the local market was quiet with prices adjusted slightly higher in line with firmer prices in Tokyo and Kobe.

At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was indicated at 116.00 U.S. cents a kg from 114.50 cents. July RSS1 was indicated at 165.50 Singapore cents (US$1.15) a kg from 163.50 cents. July TSR20 was indicated at 157.50 Singapore cents (US$1.10) a kg from 155.75 cents. - (S$1.43 = US$1) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
